title: Whole Fluted Cup and Tethered Peridioles Bird-Nest Fungus
description: One newly authored enlarged mature bird-nest-fungus fruiting body: a short thick cup-shaped peridium has a closed basal web, an irregular complete rim, real shallow vertical inner flutes and five complete rounded lenticular peridioles seated on its floor. Each peridiole retains a small whole curved funicular tether to the cup wall; these are natural spore-bearing components, not separate eggs, seeds or counted props. All cup, lens and cord geometry is new, not an old funnel mushroom with its stem shortened, a cropped liverwort gemma cup, an earthstar sac with its rays removed, or a rearranged nest prop. One complete visible fruiting-body model and zero scenes, not the entire underground mycelium or a cluster. Four quiet opaque solid PBR roles with actual low wall relief, no texture cards or transparency. Generic enlarged Cyathus-like exterior art, not exact species, natural biological scale, precise peridiole count, microscopic spores, wall histology, hair fibres or splash-release dynamics. The top is genuinely open; no missing cutaway face is presented as a whole shell. Finite basal and peridiole seats are presentation contacts, not a physical stability simulation. No edibility, toxicity, treatment, harvesting, cultivation, medical, animation or interaction claim.
